sentences.text: Previous experiments indicated that long-term fear memory can form even when short-term memory is not measurable, challenging the assumption that long-term memory depends on short-term memory.
To investigate this, researchers used light-based tools to activate and deactivate the enzyme CaMKII while stimulating neurons to induce a specific type of synaptic strengthening.

Although activating CaMKII in CA1 neurons triggered early synaptic strengthening and physical structural changes, this initial process did not result in the formation of long-term synaptic strengthening.
Conversely, blocking CaMKII prevented early synaptic strengthening, yet long-term strengthening and a marker of gene activity still occurred, driven by other enzymes known as CaMKK and PKMζ.
These findings suggest that long-term memory and long-term synaptic strengthening can form without the activation of CaMKII.
